opportunity: kuna's DWARF type mapper truncates ordinary C declarations to void. MAX_TYPE_DEPTH = 3 counted every hop of the DW_AT_type chain, the transparent typedef/const/volatile/restrict links included, so const char *const *, const size_t *, char *const [] and char *** all ran out of budget and fell back to void: 294 truncated sites across six -g C binaries (238 stack locals/params, 55 globals, 1 prototype parameter).
test_name: kuna-console verify_typedepth (6 two-pass e2e assertions on a new -g -O0 C fixture) + 6 hermetic guard/mapper unit tests incl. forged cyclic DWARF
root_cause: An unfaithful reduction of upstream's cycle guard, not a deliberate cap. Ghidra's DWARFDataTypeImporter.trackRecursion counts RE-ENTRIES of one DIE offset and refuses the third, which fires only on a cycle; kuna reduced it to a flat three-hop budget counted over every link, which conflates 'the same DIE again' with 'a deep but finite chain'. Raising the cap was not the fix: with no cycle detection under it, any cap is both too low for real C and unable to bound a self-referential chain.

notes: The brief's three plain-C witnesses (char **authors, idx_t *pn, mbstate_t *ps in coreutils fmt) are ALREADY correct on main: #264's strip_qualifiers reaches every prototype because cppproto is default-on and rebinds C prototypes by address. What remained, and what this PR fixes, is the cpp=false paths (stack locals, global sizing) plus purely structural depth (char *** truncates even with the qualifiers collapsed).

speed.method: interleaved off/on pairs, MINIMUM of 15 pairs, gate flipped through the live KUNA_TYPEDEPTH env bridge; the mapper runs once per binary inside `load file`, so the load-dominated surfaces are the honest ones
speed.why_flat: the guard replaces an integer compare with a BTreeMap entry per DIE hop on a walk that is a handful of hops deep and runs once per prototype/local/global at load; nothing in the decompile loop is touched
